triage.rationale: The description fully specifies the function signature, file location, detection order (worktree-local bin/ then PATH), and its consumers, leaving no material design decision open.

payload.title: Add a user-level template directory so overrides are not per-project only
payload.description: templatecmd resolves a template as <project_root>/.endless/templates/<name>.local.tmpl, then <name>.tmpl, then the Go embed. That is per-project only: a user who wants the same handoff or guide wording across every project they work on must copy the override into each one, and re-copy it whenever a project is added. Add a user-level layer (e.g. ~/.config/endless/templates/) between the project layer and the embed, so precedence runs project .local -> project committed -> user -> embedded. Surfaced from E-2030, where gating the guide on report_gate raised the question of where a user edits shipped text.

triage.rationale: The description pins down the exact resolution order, the new precedence slot, and a concrete path shape (~/.config/endless/templates/), leaving only mechanical implementation.

payload.title: Re-arm verify scripts that drive the endless-go hook from a bare shell
payload.description: E-1962 made `hook claude` a silent no-op on an unrecognized agent harness, and a bare shell is one. Verify scripts that impersonate a session by piping into `endless-go hook claude` stopped exercising anything when it landed, without failing: half of what they assert is that the hook stays silent, and that passes against a dead hook. Confirmed in tests/tasks/e-1953-verify.sh.
payload.analysis:
# The failure is silent, which is why it survived a landing

`hook claude` returns immediately on an unrecognized agent harness (E-1962):
exit 0, no stdout, no side effects. A bare shell is unrecognized.

Any verify script that impersonates a session by piping a payload into
`endless-go hook claude` therefore stopped exercising anything the moment
E-1962 landed. Nothing announced it, because roughly half of what such a
script asserts is that the hook stays SILENT — a turn allowed to end, a
gate-off project, a subagent's return value, a `$FULL` license. Every one of
those passes against a hook that does nothing at all.

So the suite does not fail. It hollows out, and keeps reporting green.

## Confirmed instance

`tests/tasks/e-1953-verify.sh` pipes into `go_sandbox hook claude` at three
call sites and never exports `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT`. It passes from inside a
Claude session, which exports that variable to its subprocesses, and is hollow
from a plain terminal — which is where a pre-land gate is actually run.

## How it was found

`tests/tasks/e-1975-verify.sh` had the identical bug. 106/106 from inside a
session; 89 passed / 16 failed from a bare shell. Every failure was an
assertion that needed the hook to DO something; every assertion expecting
silence passed. That asymmetry is the signature.

E-1975 fixed its own script two ways, both of which apply here:

  * every hook invocation goes through a helper that sets
    `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=cli`;
  * a preflight fires one payload that MUST produce a block and fails loudly if
    it does not, so a dead hook fails at the top rather than hollowing out the
    body.

## What to decide, not just what to fix

Fixing E-1953's script is mechanical. The open question is whether driving the
hook belongs in a shared helper rather than being re-derived per script. The
failure mode is silent and the precondition is invisible in the script itself,
so the next author will reproduce it — as this one did, in a script written
specifically to be careful about it.

triage.rationale: it names the symptom (verify scripts silently stopped exercising the hook) but not how to re-arm them—e.g. spoofing a recognized agent harness identity vs. changing the hook's no-op behavior for bare shells—which is a material design choice left unstated.

fields.description: Replaces apply-on-connect in monitor.DB(). A connect compares the DB's migration version against the binary's and acts BY DIRECTION. DB BEHIND the binary: the binary needs DDL that is absent, so an INSTALLED binary auto-applies forward -- unconditional in non-self_dev, which has one binary -- while a CANDIDATE binary refuses, because it may never migrate the real ledger, which is the 2026-08-10 failure exactly. DB AHEAD of the binary: HALT, for any binary. Per ED-1570 a binary works with exactly one schema version, so there is no compatibility window to evaluate; the binary must be upgraded, and rollback is served by restoring a pre-upgrade backup (E-1942). Accepted consequence: a self_dev branch carrying an unlanded migration has its candidate hook degraded for the whole pre-land window, which reduces what E-998 exercises on precisely those branches. That is the price of never letting unlanded code mutate the production schema, and it is worth paying.

payload.reason: Superseded by the ED-1566/1567/1570 cluster and by E-1972 -- not decided against: it was correct for May 2026. Both consumers it names are gone: E-1039 is obsolete (replaced by E-1704), and E-995's 'sandbox run' consumer is itself under review for deletion as YAGNI (E-1963). Its policy is reversed too -- 'detect worktree-local bin/, fall back to PATH' PREFERS the worktree binary, while ED-1570 requires exact schema-version agreement and E-1972 inverts the preference outright: always invoke main's known-good binary, delegating to a worktree's only when verified compatible (measured 2026-08-13: 89 of 135 worktrees pinned to their own binary, all 103 worktree binaries older than main's, one of which took session tracking down machine-wide). Finally E-1704's self-re-exec moves binary choice INTO the binary, so the shared call-site helper this decision specifies solves a problem that ceases to exist. Recorded as rejected only because 'superseded' is not expressible yet (E-1920); reclassify when it is.

payload.title: Replace apply-on-connect with versioned migrations and connect-time verification
payload.description: Umbrella for the schema-governance work E-1944 decided (ED-1566/1567/1570) after the 2026-08-10 outage, in which a candidate binary wrote a column the real ledger lacked and session tracking went down for 30 minutes. Adopt pressly/goose as the source of schema, demote schema.sql to a generated documentation artifact, stop monitor.DB() applying schema on every connect, and require exact binary/database version agreement — a DB behind an installed binary auto-applies forward, a DB ahead of any binary halts. Children were filed as free-floating siblings held together only by cleans_up E-1944; this gives them a home.

triage.rationale: The description names the concrete adopted approach (goose as schema source, schema.sql demoted to generated doc, removal of apply-on-connect, exact version-agreement semantics for behind/ahead cases), leaving only child tasks to implement each stated piece.

fields.description: ED-1570 halts a binary whose schema version is behind the database. After an upgrade migrates the ledger, every long-running process still holding the old binary image — background agents, the jobs runner — halts on its next connect and dies mid-flight, which can take down tens of live sessions at once. Halting is correct and must not be relaxed, so the fix is on the other side: detect processes running a superseded binary and restart them onto the new one as part of the upgrade, rather than letting them discover the mismatch one by one. E-1704 is the surface that decides which binary a process should be running; it moves that choice into the binary itself via self-re-exec, governed by E-1972's verified-compatible policy.

payload.outcome: Filed on a false premise. A verify script is a pre-land gate, valid only immediately before its own land, in its own worktree. A landed one is spent — nothing should run it again — so tests/tasks/e-1953-verify.sh being hollow against E-1962's harness gate costs nothing and is not a defect. Project-wide regression is 'go build/vet/test ./...' plus 'just test'. The real lesson belongs to the script being written, not to the ones already landed: E-1975's own gate had the same flaw and had to be fixed because it is about to run.

payload.title: Agent-invoked session machinery resolves the real ledger by default; only human-typed commands must name the database
payload.description: Carve-out from ED-1561, which requires an agent to name --db on every command reaching a database in a self_dev project. That is right for commands an agent CHOOSES to run against the ledger, and wrong for machinery it runs mechanically every turn under a contract, because there the correct database is not the caller's judgement -- it is fixed by whatever reads the result. Such a surface pins main when given no --db, as hook/channel/tmux already do; an explicit --db still wins. The test for membership is not 'does an agent type it' but 'does something else already fix which database is correct'.

payload.title: The minimizer's invariants outrank its deduplication objective: prose is deduplicated, actionable content never is
payload.description: ED-1557 makes deduplication against what the user already has half the minimizer's job. It contradicts the invariants the moment prior replies enter the fetched context: a verify command sent two turns ago is redundant by that objective and mandatory by invariant 3, and nothing said which wins. Measured on the fixture with a populated reply history, the table, code block and command were dropped TOGETHER in 2 of 8 live runs, leaving one sentence; with precedence stated, 0 of 8. The user is reading this message, not scrolling back to reassemble it. This binds any presentation too -- a preview that truncates mid-fence breaks the same rule in the reply itself.

fields.title: The minimizer deduplicates against artifacts the user must review anyway, not against what was already said in chat
fields.description: The objective is not "cut what was already said". It is: cut what the user will have to review ANYWAY -- what session status already shows, and what is written into a task, a decision or another durable artifact. Saying it in chat too means they read it twice. An earlier chat reply is not such an artifact: chat is ephemeral and the user is reading THIS message, so restating a verify command from two turns ago is not duplication and must not be cut. Written as "already sent", with prior replies fed in as context, it deleted the table, the code block and the verify command together in 2 of 8 live runs, leaving one sentence. Prior chat replies are therefore not a deduplication source. Nothing here competes with the invariants; the objective was simply written wrong.

fields.title: Agent-invoked session machinery defaults to --db main; only human-typed commands must name the database
fields.description: Carve-out from ED-1561, which requires an agent to name --db on every command reaching a database in a self_dev project. That is right for commands an agent CHOOSES to run against project data, and wrong for machinery it runs mechanically every turn under a contract: there the correct database is not the caller判 judgement, it is fixed by whatever reads the result. endless task report is the instance -- the Stop hook that consumes its checkpoint pins main unconditionally, so any other routing puts writer and reader on different databases and the gate blocks every turn as "never reported". Such a surface defaults to main when given no --db, as hook/channel/tmux already do; an explicit --db still wins. The test is not "does an agent type it" but "does something else already fix which database is correct".

payload.title: Stop sandbox-routed decision add and update from committing a doc mirror onto the worktree branch
payload.description: A sandbox-routed `endless --db sandbox decision add` writes a decision mirror file into the WORKTREE under .endless/decisions and auto-commits it on the task branch ("Endless: add decision ED-1"). Hit twice while smoke-testing E-1920; both commits had to be reset away by hand, and a session that did not check `git log` would have landed sandbox test fixtures into main. DB writes route to the sandbox correctly, but the E-1747 doc-mirror half of the same command does not: it resolves a project root and commits there regardless of which DB the write went to. Sandbox decision IDs also start at 1, colliding with the real ledger's ED-1 and ED-2.

triage.rationale: it's unclear whether the fix should suppress the doc-mirror commit entirely when sandbox-routed, redirect it into the sandbox, or namespace sandbox decision IDs to avoid collision with the real ledger, and the description doesn't pick one.

payload.title: Stop reporting a missing column as an uninitialized database
payload.description: A query that fails because a column is missing is reported as `endless database is uninitialized ... db file: exists but has no endless schema`, which sends the reader to the wrong problem entirely. Hit on E-1920: `decision show` selected a column added by an unapplied schema change, and the message claimed the whole DB was uninitialized while `decision list` (not selecting that column) worked fine in the same second. The handler should distinguish a missing-table or missing-column error from a genuinely unschema'd file, and name the column and the change file to apply.

triage.rationale: The description names the exact bug, root cause, and required fix shape (distinguish missing-table/column errors from uninitialized-DB errors, and name the column and change file in the message).

fields.title: Route every file a sandbox-mode command writes to the sandbox, not just the DB and ledger
fields.description: `--db sandbox` isolates the DB and, since E-1729, the event ledger — but nothing else. Every other file a command writes still resolves a REAL project root and git-commits there. Hit on E-1920: a sandbox-routed `decision add` wrote decision mirrors into the worktree and auto-committed two junk commits onto the task branch. E-1729 already fixed this exact mechanism for the ledger and established the shape (sandbox-local dir under ConfigDir, no git commit, since a sandbox is disposable and not a repo), but it was applied at one call site instead of made a rule, so E-1747's doc mirrors re-broke it. Make the DB target govern every artifact write, so the next mirror-writing feature cannot reintroduce it.

triage.rationale: it doesn't specify the mechanism for making the DB target "govern every artifact write" (e.g., a shared routing abstraction/interface all write call sites must go through) or which call sites beyond decision/doc mirrors are in scope.

payload.title: Stop calling the SQLite database the ledger
payload.description: The db-ledger is Endless's permanent record and the SQLite database is a rebuildable projection of it, so using 'ledger' for the database conflates the two — including in the user-facing --db refusal text an agent reads when it gets the flag wrong. 31 sites in live code, docs and templates; the 80 in tests/tasks/*-verify.sh are deliberately out of scope, being spent pre-land gates.
payload.analysis:
# "Ledger" already means something else

The db-ledger (`.endless/db-ledger/*.jsonl`) is the permanent record of task
state; the SQLite database is a rebuildable projection of it. CLAUDE.md says so
in its own words. Using "ledger" for the database collapses the distinction that
architecture rests on, and it does it in the two places most likely to mislead:
agent-facing comments, and the user-facing `--db` refusal.

## Scope

31 sites in live code, docs and templates. Two are user-facing:

    src/endless/config.py:328   "  --db main     the real ledger — managing the project"
    src/endless/cli.py:302      "--db main (the real ledger) or --db sandbox (this worktree's test DB). "

The rest are comments, docstrings and two guide pages. `internal/monitor/db.go`
carries the most, and is where the term does the most damage — it is the file
that decides which database a process opens.

## Explicitly OUT of scope: `tests/tasks/*-verify.sh`

There are 80 more occurrences there. Leave every one of them.

A verify script is a pre-land gate, valid only immediately before its own land,
in its own worktree. A landed one is spent — nothing should ever run it again —
so its wording cannot mislead anyone and editing it is churn against an artifact
with no future. E-1975 already filed and declined a task (E-2033) that misread
this rule; do not re-derive it.

## Wording

`--db main` and `--db sandbox` already establish the vocabulary. Say "the main
database" and "the sandbox database" (or "this worktree's sandbox"). Avoid "real
ledger", "the real DB" and "the ledger" wherever the SQLite database is meant.

The user-facing strings deserve Mike's eye rather than a mechanical
substitution: the refusal text is the first thing an agent hits when it gets the
flag wrong, and it is currently the clearest statement in the product of what
the two databases are for.

triage.rationale: the description doesn't state what terminology should replace "ledger" for the database (e.g., naming for the SQLite projection, the --db refusal text, and other 31 sites) or how to distinguish it consistently from the real ledger.

payload.title: Stop auto-registering a worktree as its own project when the project walk-up misses
payload.description: Five worktrees are registered as top-level projects (names e-1944, e-1914, e-1975, e-1920, e-1733), so the walk-up in ProjectIDForPath and _project_root_for_cwd stops AT the worktree. Consequence: `esp` in a worktree resolves the worktree as its own project root and is a no-op, stranding the user. Written by monitor.ensureAutoRegisteredProject, which names by directory basename and INSERTs straight into the DB with no project.registered event, so the rows are invisible in the ledger and would vanish on rebuild-db. All five appeared only after E-2011 landed, and all five store an ABSOLUTE path while every legitimate row is home-relative, so the writer did not apply E-2011's storage form — a stale worktree-local endless-go misses at every rung of the walk and falls through to auto-register. The durable fix is a guard: auto-registration must never fire for a directory under .endless/worktrees — a worktree always belongs to its parent project.

triage.rationale: The description pins down the exact bug (worktree-under-.endless auto-registers as its own project via ensureAutoRegisteredProject), diagnoses the root cause (walk-up miss due to stale storage-form mismatch from E-2011), and states the fix precisely (guard auto-registration against paths under .endless/worktrees).

fields.title: Refuse to run a worktree binary against a main DB whose schema it cannot read
fields.description: The e-2011-home-relative-project-paths change file was applied to the shared main DB at 2026-08-20T18:17:55, converting projects.path from absolute to home-relative. In self-dev, every worktree carries its OWN bin/endless-go built at its branch point, and 114 of 156 worktrees hold a binary built before that moment. Those binaries compare a raw absolute cwd against a column that now holds ~/..., miss every rung of ProjectIDForPath's walk-up, and fall through to ensureAutoRegisteredProject — which silently registers the worktree as a project named after its directory. Zero stray rows exist before 18:17:55 and every one after it. Nothing checks that a binary can READ the database it opens: _schema_version already names every applied change, so a binary opening a DB carrying a marker it does not ship should refuse loudly instead of misreading. E-2011 is not the bug; it is the first format change to expose a standing hazard that every future one repeats.

payload.title: Stop the minimizer deleting direct answers to questions the user explicitly asked
payload.description: The user asked two explicit questions — "won't they just re-register until we fix it?" and "why did it start happening?" — and the minimizer deleted the answer to both, keeping only a side concern the user had raised in passing. The appeal pass, whose whole purpose is restoring an over-aggressive cut, deleted MORE: it dropped the appeal argument itself plus the remaining framing, leaving four disconnected fragments. Net effect: the user asked why a bug started, the session determined the cause with timestamp evidence, and the user received none of it. The failure mode looks like the minimizer scoring inline evidence blocks and causal narrative as unrequested elaboration, while scoring short factual bullets as responsive — exactly inverted when the request was itself a why-question. Worth adding to the corpus as a case where the denylist must not fire: content that directly answers an interrogative in the user's message.

triage.rationale: it names a failure mode and a corpus goal but leaves open how the minimizer/denylist should detect "content answering an interrogative" and how that rule integrates with existing scoring.

the description names the hazard but leaves open how a binary should detect and enforce version compatibility (e.g., minimum required change list, error vs. refuse-and-exit behavior, where the check lives, and how it interacts with auto-migration).

payload.title: Add a 0-based offset to task report --raw so earlier drafts are reachable
payload.description: `task report --raw` is a bare boolean flag (is_flag=True) that prints only the newest draft, so there is no way to reach an earlier one. The storage already supports it fully: session_gates keeps one relay row per turn with raw_draft, and session_gates_corpus indexes exactly those rows newest-first for scanning. Only the CLI surface is missing. Wanted: an optional 0-based offset, where --raw is the newest, --raw 1 the one before it, --raw 2 the one before that. Click supports this on the existing flag via flag_value so the bare form keeps working. Two details worth settling: an appeal turn writes a second row, so offsets count DRAFTS not turns and an appealed turn consumes two; and an offset past the end should say how many drafts exist rather than print nothing.

triage.rationale: The description names the exact mechanism (Click flag_value on the existing flag), the semantics (0-based, newest-first, counting drafts not turns), and the required error behavior for out-of-range offsets, leaving no material design decision unresolved.

fields.description: `task report --raw` is a bare boolean flag printing only the newest draft; earlier ones are unreachable from the CLI though session_gates retains every one, indexed newest-first. PRIOR ART: E-1959's analysis already designed the read surface — `report log` listing triples (id, prompt excerpt, raw/minimized sizes, label) and `report show <id>` rendering raw and minimized side by side, with the command shape settled as a restructure rather than a sibling group. Those decisions lapsed when E-1975 replaced E-1959; this task revives the minimum of them. Prefer list-then-show-by-id over an offset: an id is unambiguous, and it sidesteps the counting problem. If an offset is kept it MUST count TURNS, not drafts — an appeal writes a second row, and drafts are invisible to the user, who can only count the replies they saw.

fields.title: Restore a read surface for earlier minimizer drafts (report log / report show)
Make an appeal actually able to restore an over-cut draft, not just re-minimize it
fields.description: An appeal is sold to the agent as the recourse for an over-aggressive cut, but nothing implements that. report_cmd runs the appeal through the SAME minimize prompt with no separate prompt and no relationship to the pass it appeals, so it is simply another independent minimization whose input happens to contain an argument — free to return LESS than what it is appealing. Observed twice in one session on E-1920: the first pass dropped the answers to two directly-asked questions, and the appeal dropped those plus the appeal argument itself, leaving disconnected fragments; the agent then had no recourse left because the budget is one. No prompt wording can fix this, which is why it is a task rather than a denylist override — monotonicity is a mechanical property, like the invariant vetoes. Options: require the appeal's output to cover the spans it argues for, or present both passes and let the user pick.

triage.rationale: the description names two mutually exclusive options (enforce span-coverage vs. present both passes for user choice) without choosing between them, leaving the actual implementation mechanism undecided.

The description fully specifies the command shape (`report log` listing id/prompt excerpt/sizes/label, `report show <id>` rendering raw vs minimized) and the id-vs-offset tradeoff with a clear counting rule, leaving no material design decision open.
